strengths: The new offer has a clearer physical verb. The old upright mitten near the ruff becomes a small outward/upward cup, using the same contour. The 2350/2500/2620/2720 ms rendered samples show preparation followed by one outward turn, and the 2720/3050/3460/4100 samples hold the result. The quiet opposite hand leaves one gesture to read.

The order of the thought survives: notice, look, consider, return to the visitor, offer. The staging correction ends at 2350 ms, while the offer arrives at 2720 ms. The correction therefore supports the subject of attention without dragging the face away during the payoff.

At 390 px in both themes, the 330/790/1190/1900 ms frames now retain upward attention toward the question instead of inheriting the lateral/downward reading pose. The source derives this from actual element rectangles, and 320 px matched evidence shows the same correction without a phone-only anatomy variant.

The matched desktop 790 ms frames remain essentially the familiar sideward investigation. Adapting the composition does not replace the selected story or produce a different personality at each width.

The other hand families gain useful hierarchy: Thinking's free hand moves below its exact chin contact; Focused reads as two low separate mittens; Grateful shows two joined lower lobes rather than the old tight ruff band; Worried retains its diagonal relation; Shy's modest adjustment does not turn its gathering into the symmetric clasp.

Character.js is unchanged, and matched day/night sheets retain the same head, short body, original small hands, feet, antennae and layered wings. Better staging was obtained by posing the existing figure.

The controller keeps the surrounding question and controls static, reads layout outside frame mapping, carries the visible correction on replay, and freezes a paused pose during resize. These are useful continuity provisions; the reported tests and browser cases support their mechanics without claiming perceptual quality.

deductions.basis: The outward cup separates better in hands-day/night and at 240 px, and the final 390 px stage clearly differs from consideration. At 96–128 px in sizes-curious-investigate.png the hand remains a tiny shape against the forewing; the glasses and face still dominate. deductions.improvementCriterion: Preserve this improvement. Before making the hand do more, inspect the complete return-to-offer at the actual use size without the explanatory label. Prefer adequate character display space or a small posing comparison if a concrete ambiguity persists; do not enlarge the mitten anatomy or add a wave.

deductions.name: Phone subject cue is now correctly directed but remains visually quiet
deductions.kind: residual staging specificity, not the old directional defect
deductions.confidence: high that the previous direction conflict is corrected; medium for the remaining visual-specificity judgment
deductions.basis: The 390 px before/current 790 ms comparison and 1190/1900 ms frames show the head and eyes biased upward. The change is intentionally bounded and small, with a substantial vertical text-to-face gap; in the actual scene the glasses and consideration hand remain the strongest acting cues. The relationship is more plausible, but a precise 'reading this heading' interpretation still depends on the overall composition rather than an unmistakable eye gesture. This is not a claim that the gaze still points down or that a person failed to understand it.

Preserve the corrected upward hold and exact visitor return. Avoid adding a stronger head action or retargeting the hand until that observation identifies an actual problem.

improvementCriteria: Confirm that the 2350–2720 ms preparation/turn feels like one small offer rather than a wrist flick during silent normal-speed playback; the sampled monotonic motion alone cannot answer that.
Compare the scene at its intended use size with neutral prompts before making semantic claims about offering or reading. Record viewing size and scroll exposure.
Retain the upward consideration hold, corrected replay continuity, exact return-to-visitor timing and single finite ending.
For website use, make the first view and complete scene hierarchy deliberate. A review page's control stack need not become the website hero layout.
Preserve useful contact distinctions: Thinking's chin, Grateful's clasp, Worried's diagonal support and Shy's separate gathering. Do not enforce separation identically across every emotion.

limits: No uninterrupted normal-speed motion watched; a wrist flick, satisfying pause, ease quality, weight or joke cannot be certified from these stills and tests.
The phone comparison film uses a simplified composition with measured 390 px bearing. Actual DOM screenshots, not that film composition, support this review's layout judgments.
The full 24-emotion reel was not watched. The current all-emotion still sheet, relevant changed hand families and film metadata were inspected.
Browser cases are supplied desktop-browser/emulation evidence, not physical-phone or spoken-screen-reader validation. I did not rerun browser operations or tests.
No new unprimed-human comprehension, personal attribution, attachment or recall outcomes. Descriptive labels prime the intended interpretation.
The byte-identical rig and geometry checks concern anatomy integrity; they do not prove that every small contact or emotional distinction is perceptually clear.

workflowChanges: Record each previous deduction with a matched before/current view and an explicit disposition: corrected, reduced or retained. A corrected numeric bearing is not silently converted into proof of human comprehension.
Inspect the whole consideration-to-return-to-offer sequence rather than judging the endpoint alone; then inspect that endpoint at actual intended display sizes.
Treat responsive attention as an authored support channel with a defined release time. Preserve the semantic ending when layout changes.
Keep fixed anatomy and common timing while comparing a single hand pose family; distinguish preserved intentional contact from incidental contour congestion.
Ask continuous playback a precise question, such as whether the wrist turn reads as an offer or flick. Use the frame sequence to diagnose the answer rather than inventing one from the timeline.
